jobs.description: Postdoctoral Researcher (m/f/d) – Institute for Pharmacology and ToxicologyRef.-Nr.  601-2026Third-party fundingThe Faculty of Medicine is an integral part of the Otto-von-Guericke-University Magdeburg and cooperates with the Magdeburg University Hospital A.ö.R. in research, teaching and patient care.Your Responsibilities:We are seeking two highly motivated Postdoctoral Research Fellows to join our team investigating the molecular and cellular organization of the nervous system using cutting-edge spatial transcriptomics approaches. The successful candidates will work at the interface of neuroscience, genomics, and computational biology to map gene expression patterns across brain tissue with spatial resolution, contributing to our understanding of neural circuit organization, development, and disease.This is an exciting opportunity to join a collaborative, well-resourced research environment with access to state-of-the-art spatial profiling platforms (e.g., MERFISH, 10x Visium), advanced microscopy, and high-performance computing infrastructure.Two positions are available with complementary focus:- Position 1 — Experimental/Wet-lab focus: Designing and executing spatial transcriptomics experiments on neural tissue, including tissue preparation, probe design, imaging, and data generation- Position 2 — Computational/Analytical focus: Developing and applying computational pipelines for spatial transcriptomic data analysis, including cell-type mapping, spatial statistics, and integration with single-cell/single-nucleus datasets(Candidates with strong interest and skills spanning both areas are also encouraged to apply and may be considered for either position.)Key Responsibilities:- Design, plan, and conduct spatial transcriptomics experiments on neural tissue samples- Analyze and interpret complex spatial and single-cell genomic datasets- Collaborate with neuroscientists, computational biologists, and clinicians within and outside the group- Present findings at lab meetings, seminars, and international conferences- Prepare manuscripts for peer-reviewed publication- Contribute to grant writing and mentoring of graduate/undergraduate students- Maintain rigorous documentation and adhere to good research and data management practicesYour Profile:Essential Qualifications:- A PhD (completed or close to completion) in Neuroscience, Molecular/Cell Biology, Genomics, Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, or a related field- Demonstrated research productivity (peer-reviewed publications and/or preprints)- Strong written and verbal communication skills in EnglishFor the experimental-focus position, in addition:- Hands-on experience with molecular biology techniques (e.g., histology, immunohistochemistry, in situ hybridization, RNA-seq library prep)- Experience with spatial transcriptomics platforms (e.g., Visium, MERFISH, Xenium, seqFISH) is highly desirable- Experience with rodent or human brain tissue handling is a plusFor the computational-focus position, in addition:- Strong programming skills (Python and/or R)- Experience analyzing single-cell/single-nucleus RNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics data- Familiarity with relevant packages/tools (e.g., Scanpy, Seurat, Squidpy, STUtility) and statistical/machine learning methods- Experience with high-performance/cluster computing is a plusWe offer:- Access to cutting-edge spatial transcriptomics and imaging technology- A collaborative, interdisciplinary, and supportive research environment- Funding and support to attend international conferences- Opportunities for career development, mentoring, and grant-writing training- Work and family in harmony: Through Klinikzwerge (https://kita.med.ovgu.de/) , childcare may be available, subject to availability- Help protect the environment and enjoy discounted public transportation through a job ticket- In addition, we offer a diverse range of sports and relaxation activities as part of our workplace health promotion program- Onboarding: At the start of your employment, you will participate in our orientation program, where you will receive important information and training sessionsTerms and Conditions:- **Salary: **The salary group E 13 according to “Tarifvertrag für den öffentlichen Dienst der Länder” awaits you- **Appointment: **The position is to be filled as a full-time position, with a workload of 2,5 years, starting on 2027/01/01- Work Location: Otto-von-Guericke-Universität application:Please submit the following as a single PDF:1. A cover letter describing your research interests, relevant experience, and motivation for applying (max 1–2 pages)2. A full CV, including a list of publications3. Contact details for two–three references[online application](https://onlinebewerbungsserver.de/ApplyForm/AppStart.aspx?c=U_CD_11_3E_FB_F1_D5_60_F8_C3_189_FD_1C_D3_A9_C8_B3_A6_F9_09_FB_E3_03S_86_C4_8B_A5_B4_AF_1F_BFc_13_DE_F1_99_D3_A6_D1_9D_A4_1Dc_E5C_3A)by E-Mail:E-Mail schreiben (LzI3MKWvqJ5aDT1yMP5iqzq1YzEy)  - (Reference number: 601-2026)by Post:Otto von Guericke University MagdeburgFaculty of MedicinePersonnel Division - RecruitingReference number: 601-2026Leipziger Str. 44, 39120 MagdeburgIf you have an international vocational or academic qualification, your application must be accompanied by a certificate evaluation (https://www.med.ovgu.de/Forschung/Klinische+Studien/Patient+and+Public+Involvement/PPI_Glossar/Evaluation.html) from the Central Office for Foreign Education (KMK) (https://www.kmk.org/zab/zentralstelle-fuer-auslaendisches-bildungswesen/allgemeines-zur-anerkennung.html) . jobs.description: In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (25,8895 hrs/wk = 65%) starting in March 2027, we are looking for 1Research Associate / PhD Candidate in Cellular and Circuit Neuroscience (m/f/x)The newly established research group of Prof. Dr. Timothy Zolnik at the Faculty of Biology and Biotechnology, Ruhr University Bochum, investigates how deep cortical neurons influence cortical and thalamic circuits. Our work combines cellular electrophysiology with optogenetics, pharmacology and circuit approaches to study mechanisms relevant to attention and arousal.The PhD candidate will investigate cellular and synaptic mechanisms in defined cortical circuits, with a focus on layer 6b and its interactions with other cortical and thalamic neurons. The project centers on whole-cell recordings in acute mouse brain slices, combined with optogenetic circuit mapping and quantitative analysis.Scope: part-timeDuration: fixed-term, 3 yearsStart: starting in March 2027Apply by:  2026-10-26Your tasks:• Design and perform whole-cell patch-clamp experiments in acute mouse brain slices.• Measure intrinsic neuronal properties and synaptic responses in identified cell types.• Combine electrophysiology with optogenetic circuit mapping and pharmacological manipulations.• Perform or assist with stereotaxic viral injections and prepare tissue for recordings and histology.• Analyze, visualize and interpret electrophysiological data using quantitative methods.• Document experiments and present results in lab meetings and at scientific conferences.• Contribute to scientific manuscripts and the collaborative development of the research group.Your profile:• A completed Master’s degree (or equivalent) in neuroscience, biology, physiology, biomedical sciences or a related field (required).• Hands-on experience with whole-cell patch-clamp recordings in acute ex vivo brain slices (required).• Experience analyzing and interpreting electrophysiological data (required).• A strong interest in cellular, synaptic and circuit neuroscience, with careful experimental practice (required).• Very good written and spoken English and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively (required).• Experience with stereotaxic viral injections and/or optogenetics (desirable).• Experience with neuropharmacology, histology, microscopy and/or programming for data analysis (advantageous).https://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/bcb3e2ce063d3b51157dd677541be13e7e1957230?ref=AfA (https://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/bcb3e2ce063d3b51157dd677541be13e7e1957230?ref=AfA)

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher in Computer Vision and Multimodal AI for the Early Detection of Parkinson’s (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description: The University Hospital Bonn (UKB) is one of Germany’s leading university hospitals, combining top-level performance in medicine and research with excellence in teaching. Each year, more than half a million patients receive inpatient and outpatient care at the UKB. Around 3,500 students study medicine and dentistry here, and over 600 people are trained annually in healthcare professions. With approximately 9,900 employees, the UKB is the third-largest employer in the Bonn/Rhein-Sieg region. In the Focus hospital ranking, the UKB ranks first among university hospitals in North Rhine-Westphalia and second nationwide in terms of case mix index (case severity). In 2024, the UKB raised nearly €100 million in third-party funding for research, development, and teaching. The F.A.Z. Institute has named the UKB “Germany’s Training Champion” and “Germany’s Most Attractive Employer” for the fourth consecutive year.The following full-time (38.5 hours/week) position is to be filled as soon as possible at the Center of Neurology of the University Hospital Bonn:Postdoctoral Researcher in Computer Vision and Multimodal AI for the Early Detection of Parkinson’s Disease (m/w/d)The position is fixed-term until 30 September 2028 due to the duration of the research project.Parkinson’s disease is usually diagnosed only after substantial neurodegeneration has already occurred. Subtle changes in movement, facial expression and speech may emerge years earlier, but current clinical assessments are not designed to detect and quantify them at scale. We believe that computer vision and multimodal AI can help close this gap - and that meaningful progress requires researchers who want to apply cutting-edge methods to a major clinical challenge.Our goal is to develop objective and scalable digital tools for the early detection and monitoring of Parkinson’s disease. We combine video-based analysis of gait, balance, facial expression and limb movements with speech, touchscreen and wearable sensor data. A particular focus is on individuals with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder, who are at high risk of developing Parkinson’s disease or related neurodegenerative disorders.The group of Prof. Dr. Michael Sommerauer at the Center of Neurology at the University Hospital Bonn and the German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE) is seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher to join our interdisciplinary team.The successful candidate will take a leading role in the development of the computer vision components of bradyMX, our multimodal digital motor assessment platform. The position is embedded in the ERC-funded Re-START PD research program and offers the opportunity to work with unique, deeply phenotyped clinical cohorts and longitudinal datasets. Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (JGU) is one of the largest universities in Germany. Thanks to its location in the Rhine-Main science region, the university can unfold to its full potential and showcase its innovative power and dynamism. Its status as a comprehensive university allows for multidisciplinary learning and teaching and has great potential for internationally renowned, interdisciplinary research. Almost all of its institutes are located on a single campus close to the Mainz city center - creating a lively academic culture for researchers, teaching staff, and students from every continent.Academic staff member (Postdoc): Plant RNA BiologyThe Wachter group investigates the molecular mechanisms and biological functions of alternative RNA splicing in plants (https://mps-imp.biologie.uni-mainz.de/). Our recent work has identified novel components of the plant splicing-regulatory code, including structured mRNA elements (e.g., https://doi.org/10.1111/tpj.71060 ) and position-dependent functions of pyrimidine motifs (https://doi.org/10.1111/tpj.16739). By combining these functional studies with global profiling approaches, we are building a framework to understand and engineer alternative splicing in the context of plant development and stress responses.As a member of our international research team, you will examine the regulation and functional impact of splicing decisions controlled by polypyrimidine tract-binding proteins (PTBs), a family of key splicing regulators in plants and animals. Your work will build on our previous findings on PTB functions in alternative splicing and on recent results from ongoing transcriptome-wide approaches, including splicing pattern profiling, iCLIP, and TRIBE. You will further develop these analysis pipelines and integrate the resulting datasets to define the role of this central component of splicing control in the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana. The new insights from these mechanistic studies will be linked to physiological PTB functions we previously observed, including ABA-dependent seed germination and drought tolerance. The overarching goal of this project is to establish the molecular connections between PTB functions and key traits of stress physiology, thereby laying the groundwork for novel strategies to enhance plant resilience.
